segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So, we said that lo and la and los and las become le and les.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: The four become two. The four options of lo, la, los, las become le and les when it's to him, to her, for him, for her.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: And we said that me, te, and nos, they don't change to get these different meanings. They stay as they are.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: And we also saw that these words, me, te, and nos, can mean myself, yourself, ourselves, or each other.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So how would you say, I speak to myself?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Me hablo.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Me hablo. We speak to ourselves?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Nos hablamos.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Nos hablamos. Although of course, the more natural meaning you would probably understand from nos hablamos is we speak to each other, as nos also means each other.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Now, to get the meaning of himself, herself, themselves, lo and la and los and las become se, which is very easy to remember because it's the beginning of self. So when we want this meaning of self or selves, we get se.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So to recap: me, te, and nos, they already have the meanings included of myself, yourself, ourselves, each other.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: But these ones that change, these small words that change, lo, la, los, and las, to get the meaning of himself, herself, themselves, it's going to be se.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So let's practice it. He speaks to himself. How would you say that?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Se habla.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Se habla. You could say the word for he. What is the word for he?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Él. Él se habla.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Él se habla. She speaks to herself and clarify, use the word for she.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Ella. Ella se habla.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Ella se habla. Good. They speak to themselves?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Se hablan.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Se hablan. Se habla, se hablan. This se is not changing.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: I speak to myself?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Me hablo.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Me hablo. Good. So here we are not using se. For me, te, and nos, we have all of the meanings included in me, te, and nos. Good.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Tell me again, how is they speak?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Hablan.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good, but the accent, where is... Hablan.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: They speak to them. Now a different them, not themselves. They speak to them. This group is speaking to another group.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Les hablan.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So now we can go back to a verb like to stay. To remain was quedar. So to get the meaning of stay, you say I remain myself. So how was that?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Me quedo.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Me quedo. We remain ourselves, or we stay?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Nos quedemos.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: -ar verb.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Nos quedamos.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Nos quedamos. Good. And you stay, talking informally, you remain yourself?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Te quedas.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Te quedas. Are you staying?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: ¿Te quedas?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Aren't you staying?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: ¿No te quedas?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Why don't you stay? Why... ¿Por qué no te quedas? Good. ¿Por qué no te quedas? Good.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Let's just practice the words for emphasis as well. So you could say I am staying. What is the word for I?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Yo.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Yo. I'm staying. I'm remaining myself.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Yo me quedo.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Yo me quedo. Good. What was the word for we, not us, but we?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Nosotros.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Nosotros. So we have nosotros for we. How would you say we are staying, we are remaining ourselves?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Nosotros nos quedamos.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Nosotros nos quedamos. And if you are an all-female group, nosotros will change.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Nosotras.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Nosotras nos quedamos, if you are an all-female group. What is the word for you, in the sense of if we want to clarify or emphasize you are staying, speaking informally, not te, but...

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Tú.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Tú. Good. So how would you say you are staying, emphasizing that we mean you?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Tú te quedas.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Tú te quedas. Good.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So these were the versions actually we were practicing before with me, te, and nos. We didn't look at he stays, because actually what we needed to say he stays is he remains himself, and we didn't have that yet, but now we do.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Se, and it's queda.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good, that's it. Se queda. He stays, she stays, you stay. They stay or they remain themselves?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Se quedan.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Se quedan. Good. Querer was to want. Querer. What was I want?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Quiero.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Quiero. The e of querer splits when we put the stress on it: quiero. Now if you want to say I want to stay, you say I want to remain myself. So how is that?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Quiero quedarme.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Quiero quedarme. He wants to remain himself, or she wants to remain herself, he wants to stay, she wants to stay?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Quiere quedarse.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Quiere quedarse. She wants to stay: ella quiere quedarse. He wants to stay: él quiere quedarse. You formal want to stay: usted quiere quedarse. What if you wanted to say they want to stay, or you guys want to stay?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Quieren quedarse.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Quieren quedarse. So this could mean they want to stay or you guys want to stay. How would you clarify? Let's clarify they want to stay.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Ellos quieren quedarse.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. And what if it was a female group?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Ellas quieren quedarse.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Ellas quieren quedarse. Good. And you guys?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Ustedes quieren quedarse.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Ustedes quieren quedarse. And we said that whilst usted is formal, ustedes, the plural you, is not necessarily formal.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Quedarse is the version of the verb that you're going to find in the dictionary.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So in the dictionary, you will find quedar, and all of the different meanings of quedar, which is remain, and various other meanings actually this verb has, can be used like to fit: me queda bien, it fits me well, it suits me well. And then you will find the next entry, quedarse.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: And then you will find next to it, to stay. So when this reflexive, when this doing it to oneself carries a different meaning, it will get a different entry in the dictionary, and it's not going to be in the dictionary as quedarme, or quedarte, or quedarnos, but quedarse, because this se is also like oneself.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: No? If it's himself, herself, itself, it's also like oneself. So in the dictionary what you find is to remain oneself: quedarse. The se is written like one word.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Whenever we put se, lo, me, te, nos, one of these small words at the end of the "to" form, it's written like one word. We write it all together.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Let's practice this just with one more verb. We said that to get the sense of realize, I realize, in Spanish you say to give yourself account, which is a little bit like to take account of in English.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Now you need to look at darse cuenta, and know how to manipulate it to get the different versions of it that you might want.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So let's begin with I realize. I realize, I give myself account.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Me doy... me doy cuenta.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: That's it. Me doy cuenta. I don't realize?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: No me doy cuenta.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: No me doy cuenta. Good. We realize, or we give ourselves account?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Nos damos cuenta.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Nos damos cuenta. Perfect. We don't realize?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: No nos damos cuenta.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. No nos damos cuenta. Now we can make the other versions with he, she, it, and you formal, and they, and you guys, because we have se, so now we can do this.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So how would you say he realizes or she realizes? Go back to dar.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Da. Se da cuenta.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Se da cuenta. What if we wanted to clarify she? She realizes.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Ella se da cuenta.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Ella se da cuenta. Good. And they realize?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Se dan cuenta.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. And they don't realize?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: No se dan cuenta.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: No se dan cuenta. So this could be they don't realize or you guys don't realize. Well done.
